prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across the five frames, the scene is dominated by uneven rock and dirt immediately in front of and below the camera wearer, with vegetation and a steep drop or distant terrain near the upper edge; the repeated bright lower regions suggest nearby ground at roughly 0.5–2 m, while the darker upper regions indicate substantially greater distance. The depth map makes the near-to-far structure of the sloping surface clearer than the RGB alone and shows the camera turning across the rocky area rather than approaching a single fixed surface. Partial people appear near the top of frame 4 and along the right side of frame 5; the frame-5 person is approximately 0.5–1.5 m away and therefore within arm's reach or just beyond it, while the frame-4 person appears roughly 1–3 m away. The frame-5 person's near arm crosses leftward in front of their torso, but their distance from other partly visible people cannot be measured reliably. Depth around silhouettes, the image seams, the bright flare-like regions, and distant terrain is unreliable, so these metre estimates are coarse and the map does not reliably establish gaze or exact facing direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies almost no foreground instances in frames 1–3 despite visible rocks and belongings, then marks a person partly cut off by the top edge in frame 4 and a much larger person occupying the right side of frame 5. The size change supports the spatial reading that the frame-5 person is much closer to the camera wearer, roughly 0.5–1.5 m away, whereas the frame-4 person is farther ahead at roughly 1–3 m; the two detections occur in different frames, so their distance from each other is not directly recoverable. In frame 5, the close person's torso is on the right and an arm extends leftward toward the centre, placing part of that arm within likely reach of the camera wearer; the head and body are clipped by the right and upper boundaries. This map makes person boundaries and partial occlusion by the frame edges easier to see than in the textured RGB, but it omits the rocky ground and most objects, merges or fragments close human regions, and includes a stray unreadable class label, so object layout and gaze direction are unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is empty in frames 1–4 and produces a skeleton only for the close person in frame 5, confirming that the useful articulated figure is on the right and very near the camera wearer, approximately 0.5–1.5 m away. The yellow body joints show one arm extending leftward and slightly downward into the centre while the other upper-body geometry remains near the right edge; clustered hand keypoints at the far right place a hand above and to the right of the main arm line, with portions of the body outside the image. This representation makes limb direction, joint arrangement, and hand location clearer than the RGB, indicating a roughly sideways or oblique body orientation rather than a fully frontal pose, but it does not provide enough facial structure to determine whether the person looks at the camera wearer. The absent poses in earlier frames do not prove that no people are present, and the distorted torso polygon, disconnected hand points, missing legs, and edge clipping make exact reach, facing, and inter-person distances unreliable.
